caption:
Instagram content protection checklist: 4 things small businesses and Black-owned brands should do now that Instagram flags copies of your Reels.

On November 17, 2026, Instagram opened content protection, a tool Facebook already had. It scans Instagram and Facebook for copies of your original videos. When it finds one, you can track it, hide it from everyone, add an "original by" link back to you, or release it. In the coming weeks, Instagram will start testing detection of AI videos that reuse the words from a creator's Reels, even when the visuals are new.

Here's how to get ready:
1. Check your activity feed and the Tools section for the invite. If it isn't there, apply.
2. Protect your older Reels by hand. New ones are covered once you enroll.
3. Add your second account and any brand partners to the allow list so they don't get flagged.
4. Put your logo, colors and handle in every Reel so a copy still looks like you.

When people find your work somewhere else, it should lead them straight back to you.

At Blackwell Graphics we build logos, visual systems and websites for Black-owned businesses. DM us "CREDIT" to talk it through, or visit blackwellgraphics.com (link in bio).

caption_drafts.explainer:
Instagram content protection is now open to creators, and it matters for every small business and Black-owned brand that posts original Reels.

Instagram announced on November 17, 2026 that the tool, already on Facebook, now scans Instagram and Facebook for copies of your videos. Each alert shows how many views the copy has and how many followers the account behind it has. You decide whether to track it, hide it, add an "original by" credit link or let it go.

Instagram is also testing detection of AI videos that reuse the words from a creator's original Reel with new visuals, starting with a small group in the coming weeks.

How many of your Reels are getting views on someone else's page? Instagram content protection lets small businesses and Black-owned brands find out.

You film the tutorial, edit it at midnight and post it. A week later a repost page has it, with more views than you got. Starting November 17, 2026, Instagram scans Instagram and Facebook for copies of original videos and tells eligible creators when one appears. You can hide the copy or add an "original by" link that sends viewers back to you.

AI copies are next. Instagram will start testing detection of AI videos that reuse the words from your Reels with new visuals in the coming weeks.
